authorization.test_split: NOT OPENED; the synthetic fixtures used here contain no real events

root_cause.statement: save_checkpoint has supported format 4 since the v3 overlay landed, but nothing ever called it with architecture_version. All three trainer save sites -- best.pt, last.pt and the mid-epoch progress.pt -- passed only the format-3 positional arguments, so save_checkpoint took its early-return format-3 branch for every run regardless of the declared architecture.
root_cause.why_the_existing_tests_missed_it: tests/test_v3_checkpoint_resume.py exercises save_checkpoint directly and passes architecture_version itself, so it proved the helper correct while the production caller was not. A helper test cannot observe an argument its caller never supplies.
root_cause.observed_consequence: S1-axis is a correct v3 run whose checkpoints record architecture_version: null and omit every format-4 field. They remain valid for evaluation and weight-only initialization but cannot carry critic, replay, controller or update-counter state, so they are not an adversarial-resume source.
root_cause.blast_radius: every v3 row that would have followed, including the D1 and D2 critic arms, whose resume depends entirely on the twelve format-4 fields

fix.behaviour: Returns {} when architecture_version resolves to cbsc-zdc-v2.2 -- including when the key is absent -- which keeps save_checkpoint on its format-3 early return and every historical checkpoint byte-identical. Under cbsc-zdc-v3 it returns the full twelve-field set, with the adversarial slots null for a supervised row.
fix.derivation_point: once per run, beside provenance, so best.pt, last.pt and progress.pt cannot disagree about the run's architecture identity

rejects: a format-4 claim that omits any V4_REQUIRED_FIELDS entry
new_guard.explicitly_permits: loading a format-3 checkpoint for evaluation and for weight-only initialization; the guard governs adversarial resume only

immutability.policy: The S1 checkpoint is immutable. It is not re-stamped, re-saved, or migrated to satisfy the new guard. If a format-4 derivative is ever required it must be a new provenance-linked file with a new hash and a proved tensor equality, never a replacement of the original bytes.

tests_added.drives: train_from_config, the real production trainer entry point, not the checkpoint helper
proofs: a v3 config yields format_version 4 and architecture_version exactly cbsc-zdc-v3, for both best.pt and last.pt
architecture_version is never null on a v3 run -- the precise S1 defect
each of the twelve V4_REQUIRED_FIELDS is present, parametrized one test per field
field types are valid for a supervised row: string version, integer counters at zero, present-but-null adversarial slots, positive support_temperature
an absent or explicitly v2.2 architecture_version still writes format 3
the format-3 key set is exactly unchanged, pinned as a literal set
a v2.2 checkpoint gains no format-4 field
the helper emits exactly the required field set and carries declared envelope hash, support temperature and contract hash
a v3 save/load round trip preserves every tensor bit-exactly
a bare v3 declaration leaves the trained weights bit-identical to the v2.2 run
the only v3-only state entry is response_envelope_caps_gev and it is provably zero-length, so the subset assertion above cannot hide a behavioural change
a supervised v3 run initialized from a v3 checkpoint is itself format 4 -- the original defect one step later
a format-4 checkpoint is accepted as an adversarial-resume source
a format-3 checkpoint loads for evaluation but is rejected as a resume source
a format-4 claim missing a field is rejected
a null architecture_version is rejected even at format 4
the screening registry records S1 as format 3, non-resume, immutable

defect_found_while_writing_the_tests.defect: the first version of test_v3_and_v2_runs_agree_on_weights asserted identical state-dict key sets between a v2.2 and a bare v3 run
defect_found_while_writing_the_tests.reality: a v3 model always registers response_envelope_caps_gev; with no envelope supplied it is torch.zeros(0) and response_cap_for falls back to the v2.2 cap rule
defect_found_while_writing_the_tests.resolution: the premise was wrong, not the code. The assertion now proves the real property: every shared tensor is bit-identical, the only extra entry is response_envelope_caps_gev, and that buffer is asserted to hold zero elements. Asserting the subset alone would have let a genuine behavioural change hide behind it, so the emptiness check is a separate test.

compileall.command: python -m compileall -q src vertex scripts tests exhibition

collected_test_count_policy: The suite total is reported as measured each phase and is not hard-coded as a final expected value anywhere in the test suite.
